records.title: How can gene therapy platforms be scaled up to treat thousands of rare diseases?
records.description: The NIH’s P. J. Brooks discusses the challenges and opportunities ahead for gene therapies and gene editing for diseases of no commercial interest.

records.title: Cancer vaccine development gets complicated
records.description: Merck and Moderna’s intismeran autogene succeeded in a landmark melanoma trial, but the oncology community still has more questions than answers about the future of cancer vaccines.

records.title: From hope to adoption: an industry perspective on the maturation of new approach methodologies
Immunogenicity risk assessment of novel modalities using new approach methodologies
records.description: Novel therapeutic modalities such as cell therapies and gene editors could potentially treat many diseases, but their clinical progression is limited by unwanted immune responses. This Perspective proposes how ‘new approach methodologies’ such as computational tools and organoids can be applied to assess the immunogenicity of novel modalities, given the limited translational value of immunogenicity data from traditional animal models.

records.title: First factor XIa inhibitor nabs FDA approval for stroke prevention
The expansion of kinase drug discovery: new targets, platforms and indications
records.description: Over the past 25 years, kinase drug discovery has been one of the most active areas in pharmaceutical research and development. This article provides a comprehensive analysis of the kinase therapeutic landscape, covering drug platforms, new targeting approaches, the expanding target spectrum, approvals and clinical trends.

records.title: Histone lysine demethylases in the third decade: biology and therapeutic prospects
records.description: Histone lysine demethylases regulate gene expression and chromatin structure and help to integrate epigenetics with metabolic and immune responses. This Review discusses the diverse contributions of these demethylases to disease pathogenesis, particularly cancer, and the efforts underway to target them with small molecules.

records.title: Conditional biologics in cancer immunotherapy: mechanisms, applications and clinical progress
records.description: Conditional biologics (CBs) — protein therapeutics engineered to selectively activate within the tumour microenvironment — have the potential to increase the potency and limit the off-target adverse effects of cancer immunotherapies. This Review describes the design principles and activation mechanisms of CBs, assesses those being investigated in the clinic, and addresses ongoing challenges and future directions for the field.

records.description: Academic centres are increasingly central to advanced therapy development, but expanding clinical use will require stronger infrastructure, integrated networks and sustained regulatory and financial support.

records.title: FDA approves hepatitis B antisense drug
Translating base editors: a decade of progress from the bench to the clinic
records.description: Base editing, a gene editing technology capable of installing point mutations with high efficiency and precision, was first reported a decade ago. This Review examines the evolution of base editors and their road to clinical translation, highlighting key advances, ongoing challenges and the current clinical trial landscape.

records.title: One year of Commissioner’s National Priority Vouchers

records.description: Charlotte Deane, co-leader of the OpenBind initiative, discusses the need for more protein–small molecule binding data.

records.title: Molecular glue targets ALK resistance
Next-generation immune cell engagers for B cell depletion in autoimmune diseases
records.description: Immune cell engagers are emerging as a strategy for deep B cell depletion in autoimmune diseases. This Review examines their mechanisms, clinical development and next-generation designs, including T cell, natural killer cell and γδ T cell-engaging formats, and considers lessons from haematological malignancies to improve efficacy, safety and durability of immune modulation.

records.title: Gene therapy for rare lysosomal storage disorder nabs FDA approval
Probing the many benefits of GLP-1 receptor agonists
COPD trial wins spur broad respiratory hopes
records.description: AstraZeneca’s tozorakimab reduced disease flare ups in patients with COPD, suggesting IL-33-targeted antibodies could offer broad potential in pulmonary diseases.

records.title: Soft drugs: design principles and topical applications
records.description: Soft drugs are designed to enhance drug safety, undergoing rapid and predictable metabolic inactivation after exerting their therapeutic effect. This review provides an overview of the principles of soft drug design, highlighting examples of topical soft drugs in development, practical considerations, ongoing challenges and future directions.

records.title: Psychedelic protects against chemotherapy-induced nerve damage
The cellular landscape of druggable RNA-binding proteins
records.description: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate every step of cellular RNA metabolism, and their dysregulation contributes to many diseases. This Perspective describes the endogenous and disease-linked roles of RBPs and strategies for their therapeutic targeting, including opportunities that arise from the recent discovery of RBPs localized to the cell surface.

records.title: Drug conjugate allows cell surface payload release
From N -of-1 therapy to health-system implementation
Refining therapeutic targeting of interleukin-6 by signalling mode selectivity
records.description: IL-6-targeted therapies have transformed the treatment of autoimmune diseases, but safety concerns related to the cytokine’s homeostatic functions remain. This Review examines classic and trans-signalling, compares global and selective therapeutic strategies, and discusses how mechanistic differences may guide future development of IL-6-targeted therapies.

The evolving landscape of drug targets
records.description: Advances in areas including genomics, automation and data science, as well as the diversification of therapeutic modalities, have led to a substantial expansion of the drug target landscape in the past 25 years. This Review maps and quantifies key elements of these changes, and discusses trends in the number and type of targets through which drugs mediate their therapeutic effects, which now include ~700 biomolecules.

A translational framework for extrahepatic oligonucleotide delivery
records.description: To unlock the ‘plug-and-play’ potential of extrahepatic delivery of oligonucleotide-based drugs, the field must bridge the gap between preclinical promise and clinical reality. Here, we outline an industry-grade quality framework to eliminate methodological artifacts and ensure the translational and commercial viability of novel platforms.

records.title: Un-siloed biomedical opportunities
records.description: Edith Heard, CEO of the Francis Crick Institute, discusses the need to break down biomedical boundaries.

records.title: Strengthening muscle for healthy ageing: innovative treatments for sarcopenia
records.description: There are currently no approved therapies for sarcopenia, the age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass and strength. This Review discusses advances in understanding of the cellular, molecular and metabolic mechanisms driving muscle wasting with ageing, while assessing emerging therapeutic approaches and agents in development.

records.title: Newest glue degrader nabs multiple myeloma approval
Click chemistry platform enhances ADC tumour targeting
Solute carrier membrane transporters: emerging targets in CNS disorders
records.description: Solute carrier transporters are critical for maintaining central nervous system homeostasis, and their dysregulation is implicated in neurological diseases. This Review discusses the roles of solute carriers in neurodegenerative diseases, autism spectrum disorders and epilepsy, highlighting therapeutic strategies to modulate their activity, emerging technologies and tools to aid drug development as well as agents currently in clinical trials.

Towards precision psychiatry: initial foundations and future directions
records.description: Drug discovery for psychiatric disorders is a slow and challenging process, driven in part by reliance on symptom-based diagnostic criteria that fail to capture the underlying disease biology. In their Perspective, Etkin and co-authors suggest a framework for a precision psychiatry approach, drawing on examples from oncology and neurology and providing initial examples for proof of principle. They discuss important biomarkers that could be used to define patient subpopulations for clinical trials and provide mechanism-based readouts to expedite psychiatric drug development.

records.title: Targeting CDKs in the RNAPII transcription cycle
records.description: Transcriptional CDKs coordinate gene expression throughout the transcription cycle and are increasingly recognized as therapeutic targets. This Review examines their roles in cancer-associated transcriptional dysregulation and highlights emerging strategies to modulate transcriptional CDKs for therapeutic benefit.

records.title: Oncolytic virus nabs FDA approval
Orexin receptor agonist secures landmark narcolepsy approval
records.description: As Takeda’s oveporexton (Orzeyful) becomes a first-in-class treatment for narcolepsy type 1, industry eyes broader indications for orexin receptor agonists.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in drug discovery — what it is, where we stand and the path forward
records.description: Applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in drug discovery have attracted high interest in recent years, but evidence for clinically relevant impact so far is limited. This Perspective discusses potential reasons, including an insufficient focus on clinical translation during model development and difficulties with applying AI algorithms on conditional life science data, and provides recommendations for the development of AI in drug discovery.

Targeting T follicular helper cells for lifelong health
records.description: T follicular helper (T FH ) cells support B cell function to promote long-lasting antibody responses but are implicated in many diseases and undergo age-related changes. This Review explores emerging therapeutic strategies to modulate T FH cells, including boosting their function for vaccination and infectious disease or limiting it in autoimmune disease, cancer and allergy.

records.title: The changing face of UK academic drug screening in the past decade
Brain-shuttle biologics chart new paths across the blood–brain barrier
records.description: Efforts intensify to ferry large-molecule medicines into the brain, following the first FDA approval of an engineered biologic that overcomes delivery hurdles.

records.title: Design, simulate, refine: simulation-guided clinical trials for accelerated drug development
records.description: Simulation-guided clinical trial design can enable identification of the optimal design to bring safe and effective therapies to patients as efficiently as possible, and it is particularly useful when exploring innovative strategies such as adaptive designs and master protocols. This Perspective discusses the value of trial simulations from the perspective of different stakeholders involved in drug development, presents best-practice recommendations, and highlights case studies that illustrate the impact of the approach.

records.title: Multispecific T-cell engagers attract cancer drug developers
records.description: Multispecific T-cell engagers that bind three or more targets on cancer and immune cells promise to address the shortcomings of their bispecific predecessors.

records.title: The unglamourous AI wins that are quietly transforming drug discovery and development
records.description: David Reese, Amgen’s inaugural Chief Technology Officer, discusses how inconspicuous AI achievements stand to transform drug discovery.

records.description: The ongoing outbreak of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo highlights the urgent need to bridge therapeutic gaps for non-Zaire ebolaviruses by prioritizing and accelerating development and evaluation of broadly applicable and species-specific filovirus countermeasures.

records.title: Understanding Ras inhibitor resistance
Inhibiting Nipah virus
Inhibiting lactate transport reduces lung fibrosis
Informing HIV vaccine design
Towards mRNA therapeutics 2.0
records.description: mRNA technology is being applied to develop a new generation of therapies for rare and common diseases. This Review discusses insights from clinical studies on mRNA-based therapeutics, including enzyme replacement therapies, cancer immunotherapies, genome-modifying therapies and immune cell reprogramming therapies, which illustrate how technological advances are paving the way for the wider adoption of mRNA technology in drug development.

records.title: Better data for better medicines: a path to data-driven medicines regulation
records.description: Over the last decade, progress in science and technology has not only spurred biomedical innovation but has also led to an exponential growth in healthcare and regulatory data. When such data are carefully managed, they can inform medicines developers and regulators to further improve decision making and accelerate medicines innovation, to the benefit of patients.

records.title: Closing the paediatric gap in cancer drug development: a call to industry
records.description: Despite transformative advances in adult oncology, children with cancer remain systematically underserved by drug development pipelines. We argue that sequential, siloed paediatric development is no longer defensible. Integrating paediatric considerations from drug discovery onwards, and leveraging tumour-agnostic trial designs, regulatory frameworks and adaptive methodologies, offers sponsors superior science, cleaner regulatory pathways and broader patient impact.

records.title: A guide to effective drug development through nonprofit models
records.description: Patient organizations are reshaping rare disease drug development where conventional systems falter by integrating patient expertise, scientific stewardship, R&D infrastructure and cross-sector coordination to unlock therapeutic progress. Drawing on a global survey, interviews and practical experience, we propose a guide for strategically directing resources toward drug development goals.

records.title: Targeting claudins in cancer
records.description: Claudins are emerging as clinically actionable targets in cancer, exemplified by the approval of CLDN-18.2-directed therapy. This review examines the biological basis and therapeutic exploitation of claudins, highlighting diverse targeting modalities and the shift towards leveraging tight junction components as tumour-selective entry points for precision oncology strategies.

records.title: Incretin-based multi-agonist reverses obesity and diabetes
FDA approves first-in-class hypertension drug
Twenty years of induced pluripotent stem cells
records.description: Nobel laureate Shinya Yamanaka discusses the therapeutic and drug discovery applications for induced pluripotent stem cells.

records.title: Realizing the potential of agonistic antibody immunotherapy
records.description: Agonistic antibodies initiate signalling by the receptors they target, mimicking the activities of native ligands. This Review discusses the clinical successes and failures of agonistic antibodies and explains how recent mechanistic insights should broaden the scope and improve the safety and efficacy of immunotherapies based on these agents.

records.title: Autophagy modulation in cancer
records.description: Autophagy has a highly complex and context-dependent role in cancer, challenging the development of autophagy-modulating strategies. This Review discusses the potential of targeting autophagy to counteract malignant transformation, prevent disease progression and enable anticancer immunosurveillance. Existing and emerging pharmacological strategies and the associated limitations are critically presented.

records.title: Trends in the landscape of clinical trials of innovative drugs in China since 2015
The evolving landscape of obesity pharmacotherapy
records.description: Incretin-based therapies are transforming the treatment of obesity and related comorbidities. This Review outlines the current landscape of obesity drug development, focusing on glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, multi-receptor agonists, amylin receptor agonists and next-generation oral therapies. Key translational and biological challenges, as well as emerging treatment concepts, are discussed.

records.description: The potential for drug repurposing to provide faster, cost-effective ways to address unmet medical needs remains to be fully realized. Overcoming systemic challenges and promoting collaboration will be key for drug repurposing to contribute more to new treatments, especially for rare diseases.

This Review assesses approaches and agents aimed at therapeutically modulating kinases, comparing orthosteric, allosteric and induced-proximity strategies. Key obstacles and future directions are considered.

records.title: In vivo CAR T purchase spree continues with Lilly deal worth up to US$7 billion
The evolving landscape of CDK inhibitor use in breast cancer therapy and beyond
records.description: Ten years after the first FDA approval, CDK inhibition is entering a new phase in oncology. This Review examines how combination strategies, emerging CDK2- and CDK4-selective inhibitors, and developing biomarkers are reshaping the clinical use of CDK-targeted therapies and broadening their potential beyond breast cancer treatment in multiple tumour types.

records.title: Inhibiting the integrated stress response restores cognition
Cell surface SRC flags tumours
Biologic degraders push forward in the clinic
records.description: A handful of antibody-based extracellular targeted protein degraders are advancing in the clinic, highlighting emerging opportunities to destroy disease-linked proteins in cancer and autoimmunity.

records.title: Safety considerations for cereblon-recruiting targeted protein degraders
records.description: Targeted protein degraders that recruit the E3 ligase CRBN are showing promise for challenging drug targets but can have unintended consequences on cellular proteins. This Perspective discusses potential toxicity mechanisms and outlines key safety considerations for the development of these therapeutics.

records.title: Target identification and assessment in the era of AI
records.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is playing an increasingly important role in drug target identification and assessment, based on its proficiency in analysing large datasets and biological networks. This article reviews advances in the application of AI-driven approaches for therapeutic target exploration, and discusses how to address challenges and limitations in the field.

records.title: Realizing the promise of CAR-T cell therapies for autoimmune diseases
records.description: Initial clinical data indicate that CAR-T cell therapies that deplete B cells could change the treatment paradigm in refractory B cell-driven autoimmune diseases. This article discusses key considerations in realizing the potential of such therapies.

records.title: FDA new drug approvals in Q1 2026
Where are the women’s health drugs?
records.description: Wendy Young, an advisor at Google Ventures and former head of small-molecule drug discovery at Genentech, discusses the dearth of women’s health drug discovery programmes.

records.title: Unlocking biological barriers: nonclinical safety considerations for RNA-based complex biologics
records.description: Bioconjugated oligonucleotides (BCOs) promise to expand the applicability of RNA-based medicines. Here, we present recommendations for nonclinical safety strategies in advancing BCOs into the clinic.

records.title: Lipid nanoparticles deliver to the pancreas
FDA approves GLP-1 pill for obesity
Dialling up the circadian clock to target ageing
The expanding role of formulations to enable oral delivery of poorly water-soluble drugs
records.description: The oral delivery of small-molecule drugs with poor aqueous solubility represents an ongoing drug development challenge. Amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) and lipid-based formulations (LBFs) have emerged as effective approaches to address this. This Perspective provides an overview of the design of ASDs and LBFs and examines the mechanisms underlying their enhanced bioavailability. Preclinical, clinical and commercialization considerations, as well as next-generation oral formulations, are discussed.

records.title: ROCK2 is a druggable angiocrine target in liver fibrosis
A renaissance in targeting the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway
records.description: The PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway represents an attractive drug target, but only a limited number of compounds have gained US Food and Drug Administration approval. This Perspective assesses existing class I PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway inhibitors, highlighting lessons learned and ongoing drug development challenges. Emerging novel classes of pathway modulators, beyond the classical reversible ATP-competitive inhibitors, are focused upon.

Can a first disease-modifying osteoarthritis drug make it past the FDA?
records.description: Biosplice says its dual CLK and DYRK kinase inhibitor reduces pain and slows joint damage. Up and coming localized gene therapies have the same goal.

records.title: Wearable technologies in clinical trials for drug development: trends and emerging opportunities
records.description: Wearable technologies, which provide new tools to capture physiological and behavioural endpoints in real-world settings, are increasingly being integrated into clinical trials. This Review summarizes the characteristics of different classes of established wearable technologies and analyses their use in interventional drug trials, as well as discussing the evolving regulatory landscape and emerging sensing technologies that could expand the scope of digital biomarkers.

Dose-finding and optimization in drug development for rare diseases
records.description: Determining the dose of a drug that is most likely to be effective and safe is a key part of any drug development programme, but is a particular challenge for drugs for rare diseases because so few patients are involved in clinical trials. Here, we discuss approaches to address this challenge.

records.title: The therapeutic potential of orphan adhesion G-protein-coupled receptors
records.description: Adhesion G-protein-coupled receptors (aGPCRs) have been implicated in multiple human pathologies, yet no drugs targeting these receptors are currently approved. This Review provides an overview of the roles of aGPCRs in health and disease, providing insight into aGPCR structure–function relationships and their diverse signalling mechanisms. Emerging strategies and compounds aimed at therapeutically modulating aGPCRs are presented.

records.title: Therapeutic targeting of neuroimmune mechanisms in neurodegeneration
records.description: Neuroimmune interactions shape neurodegenerative disease progression. This Review examines how microglia integrate signals from central and peripheral immune cells, outlines emerging therapeutic targets beyond core pathology, and discusses the growing need for immune-based biomarkers in Alzheimer’s disease and related disorders.

records.title: Approvals by the China NMPA in 2025
PD1 blockers work best when used in the morning, suggests cancer chronotherapy trial
2025’s FDA approvals by regulatory designations

Unlocking the potential of disease prevention through regulatory science
records.description: Proactive disease prevention must play a larger role in public health strategies. This will require enhanced efforts to enable the development and use of preventive medicines at scale, for the right patient group at the right time. Here, we describe regulatory and drug development recommendations to help unlock the potential of disease prevention.

records.description: Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) drives oncogene amplification, tumour evolution and therapy resistance across cancers. This Review summarizes advances in ecDNA biology, highlights emerging therapeutic vulnerabilities and outlines strategies to improve ecDNA detection and translate ecDNA-targeted approaches from bench to bedside.

records.title: Accelerating the drug regulatory process through a federated cloud ecosystem
records.description: Cloud-based regulatory platforms are transitioning from pilots to practical solutions. Sustainable adoption now relies on global coordination, continued trust and a shift towards federated, interoperable models.

records.title: Olfactory receptor activation overcomes obesity
The Biomarkers Consortium: 20 years of advancing precision medicine
records.description: The Foundation for the National Institutes of Health Biomarkers Consortium is celebrating two decades of advancing biomarker science to enable earlier interventions, personalized medicine and improved outcomes in disease prevention, detection, diagnosis and treatment.

records.title: Hunting for biopharma’s innovation sweet spot
records.description: William Pao — a former chief development officer at Pfizer and head of Roche pharma research and early development — discusses his book Breakthrough , about biopharmaceutical innovation.

records.title: Strategies for blood–brain barrier rejuvenation and repair
records.description: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) is a dynamic interface that tightly regulates the transport of substances from the blood into the brain. BBB dysfunction can occur with ageing and is a hallmark of many major diseases but is underappreciated as a therapeutic target. Here, Searson and Banks review studies on BBB repair and rejuvenation, highlighting common mechanisms across disorders and potential strategies for pharmacological intervention.

records.title: Roads and detours for CAR T cell therapy in autoimmune diseases
records.description: Following on from its success in eradicating malignant B cells in cancer, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has been extended to treat autoimmune diseases. This Review discusses the preclinical studies and ongoing clinical trials of CAR T cells in autoimmune disorders, highlighting future opportunities and challenges.

records.title: Soft drugs: design principles and topical applications
records.description: Soft drugs are designed to enhance drug safety, undergoing rapid and predictable metabolic inactivation after exerting their therapeutic effect. This review provides an overview of the principles of soft drug design, highlighting examples of topical soft drugs in development, practical considerations, ongoing challenges and future directions.

records.description: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) regulate every step of cellular RNA metabolism, and their dysregulation contributes to many diseases. This Perspective describes the endogenous and disease-linked roles of RBPs and strategies for their therapeutic targeting, including opportunities that arise from the recent discovery of RBPs localized to the cell surface.

records.description: Advances in areas including genomics, automation and data science, as well as the diversification of therapeutic modalities, have led to a substantial expansion of the drug target landscape in the past 25 years. This Review maps and quantifies key elements of these changes, and discusses trends in the number and type of targets through which drugs mediate their therapeutic effects, which now include ~700 biomolecules.

Here, we outline an industry-grade quality framework to eliminate methodological artifacts and ensure the translational and commercial viability of novel platforms.

records.description: Edith Heard, CEO of the Francis Crick Institute, discusses the need to break down biomedical boundaries.

records.title: Strengthening muscle for healthy ageing: innovative treatments for sarcopenia
records.description: There are currently no approved therapies for sarcopenia, the age-related loss of skeletal muscle mass and strength. This Review discusses advances in understanding of the cellular, molecular and metabolic mechanisms driving muscle wasting with ageing, while assessing emerging therapeutic approaches and agents in development.

records.description: Solute carrier transporters are critical for maintaining central nervous system homeostasis, and their dysregulation is implicated in neurological diseases. Towards precision psychiatry: initial foundations and future directions
records.description: Drug discovery for psychiatric disorders is a slow and challenging process, driven in part by reliance on symptom-based diagnostic criteria that fail to capture the underlying disease biology. In their Perspective, Etkin and co-authors suggest a framework for a precision psychiatry approach, drawing on examples from oncology and neurology and providing initial examples for proof of principle. They discuss important biomarkers that could be used to define patient subpopulations for clinical trials and provide mechanism-based readouts to expedite psychiatric drug development.

records.title: Targeting CDKs in the RNAPII transcription cycle
records.description: Transcriptional CDKs coordinate gene expression throughout the transcription cycle and are increasingly recognized as therapeutic targets. This Review examines their roles in cancer-associated transcriptional dysregulation and highlights emerging strategies to modulate transcriptional CDKs for therapeutic benefit.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in drug discovery — what it is, where we stand and the path forward
records.description: Applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in drug discovery have attracted high interest in recent years, but evidence for clinically relevant impact so far is limited. This Perspective discusses potential reasons, including an insufficient focus on clinical translation during model development and difficulties with applying AI algorithms on conditional life science data, and provides recommendations for the development of AI in drug discovery.

records.description: T follicular helper (T FH ) cells support B cell function to promote long-lasting antibody responses but are implicated in many diseases and undergo age-related changes. This Review explores emerging therapeutic strategies to modulate T FH cells, including boosting their function for vaccination and infectious disease or limiting it in autoimmune disease, cancer and allergy.

records.title: Design, simulate, refine: simulation-guided clinical trials for accelerated drug development
records.description: Simulation-guided clinical trial design can enable identification of the optimal design to bring safe and effective therapies to patients as efficiently as possible, and it is particularly useful when exploring innovative strategies such as adaptive designs and master protocols. This Perspective discusses the value of trial simulations from the perspective of different stakeholders involved in drug development, presents best-practice recommendations, and highlights case studies that illustrate the impact of the approach.

records.description: mRNA technology is being applied to develop a new generation of therapies for rare and common diseases. This Review discusses insights from clinical studies on mRNA-based therapeutics, including enzyme replacement therapies, cancer immunotherapies, genome-modifying therapies and immune cell reprogramming therapies, which illustrate how technological advances are paving the way for the wider adoption of mRNA technology in drug development.

records.title: Better data for better medicines: a path to data-driven medicines regulation
records.description: Over the last decade, progress in science and technology has not only spurred biomedical innovation but has also led to an exponential growth in healthcare and regulatory data. When such data are carefully managed, they can inform medicines developers and regulators to further improve decision making and accelerate medicines innovation, to the benefit of patients.

records.title: Closing the paediatric gap in cancer drug development: a call to industry
records.description: Despite transformative advances in adult oncology, children with cancer remain systematically underserved by drug development pipelines. We argue that sequential, siloed paediatric development is no longer defensible. Integrating paediatric considerations from drug discovery onwards, and leveraging tumour-agnostic trial designs, regulatory frameworks and adaptive methodologies, offers sponsors superior science, cleaner regulatory pathways and broader patient impact.

records.title: A guide to effective drug development through nonprofit models
records.description: Patient organizations are reshaping rare disease drug development where conventional systems falter by integrating patient expertise, scientific stewardship, R&D infrastructure and cross-sector coordination to unlock therapeutic progress. Drawing on a global survey, interviews and practical experience, we propose a guide for strategically directing resources toward drug development goals.

records.title: Targeting claudins in cancer
records.description: Claudins are emerging as clinically actionable targets in cancer, exemplified by the approval of CLDN-18.2-directed therapy. This review examines the biological basis and therapeutic exploitation of claudins, highlighting diverse targeting modalities and the shift towards leveraging tight junction components as tumour-selective entry points for precision oncology strategies.

records.title: Realizing the potential of agonistic antibody immunotherapy
records.description: Agonistic antibodies initiate signalling by the receptors they target, mimicking the activities of native ligands. This Review discusses the clinical successes and failures of agonistic antibodies and explains how recent mechanistic insights should broaden the scope and improve the safety and efficacy of immunotherapies based on these agents.

records.title: Autophagy modulation in cancer
records.description: Autophagy has a highly complex and context-dependent role in cancer, challenging the development of autophagy-modulating strategies. This Review discusses the potential of targeting autophagy to counteract malignant transformation, prevent disease progression and enable anticancer immunosurveillance. Existing and emerging pharmacological strategies and the associated limitations are critically presented.

records.description: Incretin-based therapies are transforming the treatment of obesity and related comorbidities. This Review outlines the current landscape of obesity drug development, focusing on glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists, multi-receptor agonists, amylin receptor agonists and next-generation oral therapies. Key translational and biological challenges, as well as emerging treatment concepts, are discussed.

This Review assesses approaches and agents aimed at therapeutically modulating kinases, comparing orthosteric, allosteric and induced-proximity strategies. Key obstacles and future directions are considered.

records.title: Safety considerations for cereblon-recruiting targeted protein degraders
records.description: Targeted protein degraders that recruit the E3 ligase CRBN are showing promise for challenging drug targets but can have unintended consequences on cellular proteins. This Perspective discusses potential toxicity mechanisms and outlines key safety considerations for the development of these therapeutics.

records.title: Target identification and assessment in the era of AI
records.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is playing an increasingly important role in drug target identification and assessment, based on its proficiency in analysing large datasets and biological networks. This article reviews advances in the application of AI-driven approaches for therapeutic target exploration, and discusses how to address challenges and limitations in the field.

records.title: Realizing the promise of CAR-T cell therapies for autoimmune diseases
records.description: Initial clinical data indicate that CAR-T cell therapies that deplete B cells could change the treatment paradigm in refractory B cell-driven autoimmune diseases. This article discusses key considerations in realizing the potential of such therapies.

records.description: Bioconjugated oligonucleotides (BCOs) promise to expand the applicability of RNA-based medicines. Here, we present recommendations for nonclinical safety strategies in advancing BCOs into the clinic.

records.description: The oral delivery of small-molecule drugs with poor aqueous solubility represents an ongoing drug development challenge. Amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) and lipid-based formulations (LBFs) have emerged as effective approaches to address this. This Perspective provides an overview of the design of ASDs and LBFs and examines the mechanisms underlying their enhanced bioavailability. Preclinical, clinical and commercialization considerations, as well as next-generation oral formulations, are discussed.

records.description: The PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway represents an attractive drug target, but only a limited number of compounds have gained US Food and Drug Administration approval. This Perspective assesses existing class I PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway inhibitors, highlighting lessons learned and ongoing drug development challenges. Emerging novel classes of pathway modulators, beyond the classical reversible ATP-competitive inhibitors, are focused upon.

records.title: Wearable technologies in clinical trials for drug development: trends and emerging opportunities
records.description: Wearable technologies, which provide new tools to capture physiological and behavioural endpoints in real-world settings, are increasingly being integrated into clinical trials. This Review summarizes the characteristics of different classes of established wearable technologies and analyses their use in interventional drug trials, as well as discussing the evolving regulatory landscape and emerging sensing technologies that could expand the scope of digital biomarkers.

Here, we discuss approaches to address this challenge.

records.title: The therapeutic potential of orphan adhesion G-protein-coupled receptors
records.description: Adhesion G-protein-coupled receptors (aGPCRs) have been implicated in multiple human pathologies, yet no drugs targeting these receptors are currently approved. This Review provides an overview of the roles of aGPCRs in health and disease, providing insight into aGPCR structure–function relationships and their diverse signalling mechanisms. records.description: Neuroimmune interactions shape neurodegenerative disease progression. records.title: Strategies for blood–brain barrier rejuvenation and repair
records.description: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) is a dynamic interface that tightly regulates the transport of substances from the blood into the brain. BBB dysfunction can occur with ageing and is a hallmark of many major diseases but is underappreciated as a therapeutic target. Here, Searson and Banks review studies on BBB repair and rejuvenation, highlighting common mechanisms across disorders and potential strategies for pharmacological intervention.

records.title: Roads and detours for CAR T cell therapy in autoimmune diseases
records.description: Following on from its success in eradicating malignant B cells in cancer, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has been extended to treat autoimmune diseases. This Review discusses the preclinical studies and ongoing clinical trials of CAR T cells in autoimmune disorders, highlighting future opportunities and challenges.
